messages:
elaine: Installed redwoodctl via snap on Ubuntu 22.04, ran `snap install redwoodctl`. Browser auth opens but callback never received and CLI says 'no profile found'. Anyone seen this with snap?

samk: snaps confine apps. Try checking under the snap user-data path: `/home/elaine/snap/redwoodctl/common/.config/redwood/` — config lives there often.

elaine: I found `token.json` under `/home/elaine/snap/redwoodctl/common/.config/redwood/token.json` but redwoodctl is expecting `~/.config/redwood/`. So it never picks it up.

priya: Two quick workarounds: install with classic confinement if the snap supports it (`snap install --classic redwoodctl`) or create a symlink from `~/.config/redwood` to the snap path.

elaine: Symlink fixed the auth callback — `ln -s /home/elaine/snap/redwoodctl/common/.config/redwood ~/.config/redwood` made `redwoodctl auth login` show `Logged in as elaine@example.com`. But now `redwoodctl local-run` can't find my profiles.

samk: local-run looks for `profiles.yaml` in the same config dir. With snap, there are multiple runtime paths (`$SNAP_USER_DATA`, `$SNAP_COMMON`) and permission differences. Snap may not follow home symlinks depending on confinement.

priya: If you need an immediate fix, use the headless/login-with-token flow: `redwoodctl auth login --headless --token-file /path/to/token.json`. We intentionally added the headless flag for CI and constrained installs. Also `redwoodctl local-run --config /full/path/to/profiles.yaml` will bypass detection.

elaine: Headless token login accepted. Local-run works with explicit `--config`. Still think we should document this — snap users will trip over it.

devex-bot: NOTE: Internal issue referenced: GH #482 (packaging: snap confinement causes config path mismatch).

priya: I'll open a small docs PR to call out snap caveats and add the symlink and `--config` examples. Also proposing an enhancement: `--config-dir` flag so redwoodctl can be explicit about where to look.

samk: +1 on the flag. Also ops: check whether our snap should write to `$SNAP_USER_DATA` vs `$HOME` and whether a `classic` channel is viable.

infra: FYI we already had one customer message about snap on Ubuntu. I'll add a packaging note for the infra checklist.

elaine: Leaving exact commands that worked for me:```bash
snap install redwoodctl
ln -s /home/elaine/snap/redwoodctl/common/.config/redwood ~/.config/redwood
redwoodctl auth login --headless --token-file ~/.config/redwood/token.json
redwoodctl local-run --config ~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml
```

elaine: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: — feel free to ping if you want me to test a docs patch or the new flag when it's available.
